title: Kernel of the nested cutoff comparison has two terms and invertible differential
statement: Let $C$ be abelian and $L$ a nonnegative cochain complex. Define the cutoffs $T_c$ and windows $W[a,b)$ by [lem-sp-double-complex-vertical-tower-maps] and [def-sp-double-complex-vertical-window]. Let $0<a<b$ be integers, $g:T_a(L)\to T_b(L)$ satisfy $g\iota_b=\iota_a$, and $q:\operatorname{coker}g\to W[a,b)(L)$ satisfy that its composite with the cokernel projection is the restriction of $\tau_{\le b-1}(E\to\tau_{\ge a}E)$, where $E$ is $L$ extended by zero to integer degrees. Then $\ker q$ is zero outside natural degrees $a-1$ and $a$, and its differential from degree $a-1$ to $a$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: homology-section-truncations, cochain canonical truncations (3) and (4); specialization of the assigned node's endpoint argument.

proof.text: Prove vanishing outside the endpoints directly. Below a-1, the two cutoff inclusions into the reextended column are invertible, so hg makes g degreewise invertible and its cokernel is zero. Above a, the lower cutoff source is zero, hence the cokernel projection is invertible. The canonical comparison is invertible there: below the upper boundary use inclusion naturality and the invertible lower projection, at the upper boundary use the cycles map of an invertible middle component and monomorphic next component, and beyond it both objects are zero. Thus q is invertible and its evaluated kernel is zero. Evaluation preserves kernels and cokernels. Reuse the proved private inclusion_f_isIso from VerticalCutoffComparisonEpi, pi_f_above from LowerTruncationTransitionKernel, and truncLEXIsoCycles_naturality from UpperTruncationStepSES through proof-only import all; the latter reuses truncLEXIsoCycles_comp_iCycles.

Apply the boundary kernel and cokernel forks. The degree-a source of g and degree-(a-1) target of q vanish by strict support. Thus the cokernel projection at a and kernel inclusion at a-1 are invertible. Transport the degree-(a-1) cokernel of g to the coimage of the upper cutoff differential, and the degree-a kernel of q to its image, using the two forks. The chain-map equations for the cokernel projection and kernel inclusion identify the remaining kernel differential with the coimage-to-image comparison. That comparison is invertible in an abelian category; cancel the conjugating isomorphisms. Combine this with the already proved vanishing statement.

lean.statement:
theorem verticalCutoff_comparison_kernel_twoTerm
    (L : CochainComplex C ℕ) (a b : ℤ) (hab : a < b) (ha : 0 < a)
    (g : (verticalCutoff a).obj L ⟶ (verticalCutoff b).obj L)
    (hg : g ≫ (verticalCutoffι b).app L = (verticalCutoffι a).app L)
    (q : cokernel g ⟶ (verticalWindow a b).obj L)
    (hq : cokernel.π g ≫ q = HomologicalComplex.restrictionMap
      (CochainComplex.truncLEMap
        (CochainComplex.πTruncGE (L.extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat) a) (b - 1))
      ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat) :
    (∀ n, n ≠ a.toNat - 1 → n ≠ a.toNat → IsZero ((kernel q).X n)) ∧
      IsIso ((kernel q).d (a.toNat - 1) a.toNat)
